title: Bound the admin user search to the acting organization
working_tree_status: dirty (676 entries; concurrent DB-017, EVENTS-001/004, ADMVIEW-001, INTG-007, MKT-004 work in flight)
goal: Restrict GET /api/admin/users/search to users the acting organization can already see, or remove the route from the core launch surface.
resume_condition: The task is selected as the owner's next collision-free work item.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-1: the handler resolves the organization from admin.orgId, never from a request body or query parameter, and pushes the visible user id list into the profiles query - or the route is registered with an explicit non-user principal.
evidence: Completion path chosen: ORG-BOUND. Code evidence for choosing it over removing the route from the launch surface: (1) the route is mounted by five live admin components that all need a person-picker scoped to the acting organization - components/admin/staff-roster-panel.tsx:88 (add member to the org staff roster), components/admin/rbac-role-assignment.tsx:63 (assign an org role), components/admin/grant-tour-admins-panel.tsx:76, components/admin/tours/tour-quick-start-wizard.tsx:137, components/admin/logistics-dynamic-manager.tsx:271; (2) the registry classifies the route capability_gated, not legacy_pending_migration, so it is a declared core-launch route and not admitted legacy debt; (3) no schema or migration is needed because the acting-admin context already carries a verified organization and a canonical organization directory service already exists (GET /api/admin/workforce/people uses listWorkforcePeople with the same admin.orgId). Removing the route would break RBAC role assignment, a P0 security surface, for no gain.

app/api/admin/users/search/route.ts:80 - the only organization input is resolveOrganizationUserIds(supabase, admin.orgId); admin comes from withAdminCapability's verified ActingAdminContext (lib/auth/api-auth.ts:284 resolveActingAdminContext), never from the request. Confirmed by the base-SHA source containing no occurrence of admin.orgId (the pre-repair handler destructured only { supabase }).

app/api/admin/users/search/route.ts:66-72 - org_id, ops_org_id and organizer_account_id are rejected with 400 organization_scope_field_rejected before any read, so a GET cannot carry a caller-chosen organization (ADMIN-013/ADMIN-015 precedent). A mismatched x-acting-org-id header is refused earlier with 403 acting_context_mismatch by the wrapper.

app/api/admin/users/search/route.ts:20-29 - the visible id list comes from listWorkforcePeople with employerEntityType 'organization' and employerEntityId admin.orgId, which binds .eq('org_id', orgId) on org_members and .eq('employer_entity_type'/'employer_entity_id', ...) on staff_members and employment_assignments (lib/services/admin-workforce-people.service.ts:92,113,144). No branch of that service is reachable with a null or absent employerEntityId, so a context without an organization returns zero rows rather than a global read.

app/api/admin/users/search/route.ts:31-61 - the id list is pushed into the profiles query itself (.in('id', userIds.slice(index, index + 100)) at line 43) in 100-id chunks with a merge, so the scope is a query predicate and not a post-read filter. The projected columns, the or(full_name.ilike, email.ilike) filter, the full_name ordering, the 1..50 limit clamp and the { users } response shape are unchanged from the base SHA.

AC-1 assertion 'the route is registered with an explicit non-user principal' was not needed: the route keeps the user principal with an organization bound at the data boundary, which is the AC-1 first branch.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-2: a cross-tenant test proves a second organization admin receives zero rows and zero email values.
evidence: __tests__/admin/admin-user-search-org-scope.test.ts, describe 'a second organization receives zero rows and zero emails': (a) a query only organization B matches returns { users: [] } and the serialized body contains neither B's user id nor cipher@orgb.test; (b) the unlinked platform profile that matches is never returned; (c) the identical query shape still returns organization A's rows, so the denial is not a broken route; (d) replayed as organization B's own admin against organization B's acting account, the route returns B's two users and none of A's emails, proving the organization is resolved from the acting context rather than a fixed id.

NEGATIVE CONTROL A (CP-104 discipline) - run and observed: the route was temporarily replaced with its base-SHA source (git show 16fb834f:app/api/admin/users/search/route.ts, sha256 fcd48002eb7f9763349751a858b589fc9f3ff813a6bf9a716194edf7b843a59) and the same file re-run. Result: 11 of 21 tests FAILED, including both core cross-tenant tests, 'pushes the organization scope into the query instead of filtering after the read', 'rejects caller-supplied organization scope parameters with 400 and no read', and 'reads a large organization scope in bounded chunks'. The removed bound returned cipher@orgb.test and outsider@platform.test verbatim. The route was then restored from a byte-exact backup and shasum -c confirmed sha256 6564cba0c76f02a9eaa76c51c74abe7f96ae5b66db90e7239ad785f35d6cb3df, and the suite returned to 21/21 green. The AC-2 assertions are therefore not a hardcoded literal over a now-false claim.

Anti-vacuity is structural, not only behavioural: the first describe block regenerates the base source with git show into a generated mirror (__tests__/admin/.admin020-base-mirror, removed in afterAll), imports it, and asserts the base route returns every platform user id with emails - so the fake client honours filters and a real cross-tenant read is demonstrable rather than assumed. afterAll also asserts the shared route file is byte-identical to what it read in beforeAll, so the proof cannot be produced by editing the shared tree.

Supporting controls in the same file: exactly 3 response rows, the four original projected columns, the ordering and limit clamp, the under-two-character short circuit, the empty-directory fail-closed path, the zod length rejection, the 400 on a failing profiles read, and a 123-user organization read in two bounded chunks that still returns the same top 12.
